items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.title: Delma Infrastructure Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Delma Infrastructure Ltd. (DIL) prepares consolidated financial statements. Its holdings:

b: Sima Developers Pvt. Ltd.: 30% equity. DIL is on the board and takes part in policy decisions.
Orion Estates Ltd.: 18% equity. DIL has a board seat, but all decisions need a 3/4th majority and DIL does not actively take part. Management says there is no significant influence.
Bela Ltd.: 25% equity, held temporarily for resale within 6 months.

items.q: Which entity/entities should DIL treat as an associate under AS 23?
items.why: An associate needs significant influence. Sima (30% + board + active policy participation) qualifies. Orion (18%, no real participation) does not. Bela is held exclusively for disposal in the near future, so it is not treated as an associate.
items.trap: Bela's 25% crosses the 20% presumption, but the intention to sell within 6 months overrides it.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Aarav Renewable Energy Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Aarav Renewable Energy Ltd. (AREL), a public company, proposes to raise ₹10 crore by issuing equity shares to 65 identified persons, including 8 Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs). It has made no other private placement during the financial year.

items.q: Which statement about AREL's proposed offer is most appropriate?
o: It is a public offer, as sec 42 caps offers at 50 persons incl. QIBs
QIBs excluded: 57 counted, within 200; other sec 42 conditions apply
All 65 count towards the 200-person limit, as QIBs are included
Not permissible, as QIBs cannot be among the identified persons
items.why: Sec 42 with Rule 14 allows a private placement to at most 200 persons in aggregate in a financial year, excluding QIBs and employees under ESOP. So 57 are counted. The other conditions still apply: no public advertisement, money only through banking channels, and allotment within the prescribed time.
items.trap: The 50-person limit is the deemed public offer test under the old law.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Aarav Sharma

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Aarav Sharma (52), an Indian citizen, is a crew member of an Indian ship in international traffic. As per his Continuous Discharge Certificate, he joined on 6 June 2025 and signed off on 5 December 2025. He has been crew since 2010. In earlier years, he was away as crew for less than 180 days a year and was in India for the rest of the year.

items.q: What is Mr. Aarav's residential status for P.Y. 2025-26?
items.why: For an Indian citizen who is crew of an Indian ship, the period from joining to signing off as per the CDC (6 June to 5 Dec = 183 days) is excluded from his stay in India. Stay = 365 − 183 = 182 days, so he is resident. In earlier years he stayed over 182 days each year, so he is ROR.
items.trap: Count the days. Do not assume a crew member is non-resident.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.topic: Place of supply – accommodation in many States
items.title: Aravali Ventures Pvt. Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Aravali Ventures (registered in Rajasthan and in every State where it operates) sells a 'Golden Triangle' hotel package for ₹90,000: 5 nights in Jaipur (Rajasthan), 3 nights in Agra (UP) and 1 night in Delhi. The contract has no city-wise price split.

items.q: What is the place of supply, and the value attributable to Rajasthan?
o: All three States in ratio of nights (5:3:1); ₹50,000
Location of recipient; value cannot be ascertained
items.why: Sec 12(3) IGST: accommodation in more than one State for a single price is treated as supplied in each State. With no split in the contract, value is apportioned in the ratio of nights: 5/9 × 90,000 = ₹50,000.
items.trap: An equal split ignores the prescribed basis, which is the number of nights.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.title: Kaveri Consumer Durables Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Kaveri Consumer Durables Ltd. analyses customer profitability using ABC. Customer visits cost ₹10,800 per visit. During the year: Sahyadri (SEM) – 2 visits, Deccan (DHA) – 3 visits, Konkan (KDW) – 6 visits, Shivneri (SRH) – 3 visits.

items.q: What is the cost of customer visits for Shivneri Retail Hub (SRH)?
items.trap: ₹21,600 is SEM's figure. Pick the right customer.

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: Arnav Engineering Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Arnav Engineering (listed) processes many sales through its ERP. Reliable monthly data is available by product and region, collections follow a consistent pattern, and historical relationships are stable. However, some year-end balances arise from unusual transactions and involve significant estimates.

items.q: What is the most appropriate approach for revenue and receivables?
o: Analytics are never appropriate for balance sheet accounts
Analytics suffice whenever data is reliable, despite estimates
Analytics suffice where relationships are stable; no detail tests
Analytics may suit reliable data, subject to the assessed risks
items.why: Substantive analytics work well where data is reliable and relationships are predictable. Unusual transactions and significant estimates still need responses based on the assessed risks.
items.trap: 'Sufficient on their own' is too strong, given the unusual items.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Solaris Components Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Solaris Components (equity beta 1.20) is evaluating a riskier EV-charging business. Listed EV-charging companies have an equity beta of 1.50, which already reflects business and financial risk. Risk-free rate 7%; market risk premium 6%.

items.q: What is the cost of equity appropriate for the EV project?
items.why: Use the project's own beta: Ke = 7% + 1.50 × 6% = 16.0%.
items.trap: 14.2% uses Solaris's own beta of 1.20.

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: Garud AI

caseBlocks.p: Garud AI (Bengaluru) grew fast and merged with Technova Systems in 2025. CEO Arjun Mehta first focused on clear targets and incentives, then shifted to innovation, employee empowerment and a shared vision. This culture of creativity carried the company smoothly through the merger.

items.q: What underlying factor supported the smooth cultural transition?
o: Inbuilt value system of the company
items.why: Mehta moved from a transactional style (targets, incentives) to a transformational one (vision, empowerment, innovation). That leadership sustained the culture.
items.trap: A shared vision is a tool the transformational leader uses. It is not the underlying factor.

items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.title: Anshul Manufacturers

caseBlocks.p: Anshul Manufacturers bought 20,000 kg of raw material @ ₹170 per kg. The price includes ₹15 per kg GST, for which full input tax credit will be availed. Direct transit cost: ₹5,00,000. Normal transit loss: 3%. Quantity received: 19,000 kg.

items.q: What will be the total cost of material?
items.why: (170 − 15 GST credit) × 20,000 = 31,00,000 + transit 5,00,000 = ₹36,00,000. Recoverable taxes are excluded from cost under AS 2.
items.trap: ₹39,00,000 includes GST that will be recovered as ITC.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Mr. A's proposed LLP

caseBlocks.p: Mr. A wants to form an LLP with Mr. X, Mr. B and Mr. C. All have consented to act as designated partners. Their stay in India during the previous financial year: X – 170 days, B – 110 days, C – 100 days.

items.q: Which combination of designated partners would NOT comply with the LLP Act, 2008?
o: Mr. X, Mr. B and Mr. C
items.why: Sec 7 requires at least two individual designated partners, at least one of whom is resident in India, meaning a stay of 120 days or more in the financial year. Only Mr. X qualifies.
items.trap: The test is 120 days (post-2021), not the 182 days used in income tax.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Saksham

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Saksham's life insurance policies:
Maturity proceeds: X ₹7,00,000; Y ₹36,00,000; Z ₹28,00,000; A ₹30,00,000. B is a term policy.

items.q: Maturity proceeds of which policies qualify for exemption u/s 10(10D)? (choose the most beneficial option)
items.why: X (2017, premium 8% of sum assured, within 10%) is exempt. For policies issued on or after 1.4.2023, exemption is available only while the aggregate premium is within ₹5 lakh. Y + Z + A = ₹7.5 lakh, so the best combination within ₹5 lakh is Y + Z (highest proceeds).
items.trap: Z + A (₹4.5 lakh) also fits the limit, but gives lower exempt proceeds.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.topic: Time of supply – cessation of service
items.title: Ganesh & Sons

caseBlocks.p: On 20-03-2025, Ganesh & Sons (Odisha) agreed to paint a client's office for ₹2,00,000, to be completed by 20-04-2025. After a dispute, the work stopped on 31-03-2025 with 60% completed.

items.q: What is the due date of the invoice, and its value?
items.why: Sec 31(6): when a service ceases under a contract before completion, the invoice is issued at the time of cessation (31-03-2025), to the extent of supply made (60% × 2,00,000 = ₹1,20,000).
items.trap: The full contract value doesn't matter once the work stops midway.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.title: Alpha Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Alpha Ltd., Process P (April 2026): 10,000 kg of material @ ₹5 issued. Direct material ₹38,000; direct labour ₹30,000. Production overheads ₹90,000 are absorbed on total direct labour of ₹1,20,000 across all processes. Normal wastage 10% of input; scrap ₹1/kg. Output transferred to Q: 9,000 kg.

items.q: What is the cost per kg of output transferred from Process P?
items.trap: ₹15.61 ignores the scrap value of normal wastage.

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: MNO Hospitality Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: MNO Hospitality's weekly trading accounts show large gross profit swings in two restaurants. Management blames 'seasonal factors' without evidence. Kitchen Order Tickets (KOTs) are not consistently preserved, and only some bills can be traced.

items.q: What is the most appropriate audit response?
o: Rely on management, as weekly trading accounts are prepared
Ignore it, as hotel margins are naturally volatile
Extend substantive tests; consider modifying the opinion
Restrict the audit to test checks due to practical limits
items.why: Unexplained GP swings with missing primary records raise the risk of material misstatement. Extend substantive work. If issues remain unexplained, consider a modified opinion (SA 705).
items.trap: Unsupported management explanations are not audit evidence.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Orion Manufacturing Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Orion's machine X-Pro costs ₹20,00,000 (5-year life, straight-line depreciation, no salvage, tax 30%). Annual savings: wages ₹7,00,000 and scrap ₹60,000. Extra annual costs: indirect material ₹30,000, indirect labour ₹40,000, repairs ₹45,000.

items.q: What is the payback period of X-Pro?
items.trap: Using pre-tax savings understates the payback.

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: Pharma company

caseBlocks.p: A multinational pharma company aspires to become 'the world's most trusted innovator in affordable healthcare by 2045'. It first identifies broad future outcomes, such as strengthening global presence and enhancing research, and then translates them into specific, measurable targets.

items.q: The broad future outcomes are best described as:
items.why: Goals are broad, open-ended outcomes the organisation wants to achieve. Objectives are their specific, measurable and time-bound form.
items.trap: The 2045 aspiration is the vision. The broad outcomes are goals.

items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.title: Building revaluation

caseBlocks.p: A company revalues its building, increasing the carrying amount by ₹5,00,000. In an earlier year, the same building had been written down by ₹2,00,000 on revaluation, and that decrease was charged to the Profit and Loss Statement.

items.q: As per AS 10, how should the current increase of ₹5,00,000 be treated?
o: ₹2,00,000 to P&L (reversal) and ₹3,00,000 to Revaluation Reserve
Entire ₹5,00,000 credited to the Profit and Loss Statement
Ignored, as revaluation increases are not recognised
items.why: Under AS 10, a revaluation increase is credited to P&L to the extent it reverses a decrease previously charged to P&L for the same asset (₹2,00,000). The balance (₹3,00,000) goes to Revaluation Reserve.
items.trap: Crediting the full amount to reserve ignores the earlier loss that went through P&L.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Aarav Renewable Energy Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: AREL held its previous AGM on 30 September 2025. For the financial year ended 31 March 2026, the Board proposes to hold the next AGM on 31 December 2026, saying it needs time to finalise accounts. No extension has been granted by the ROC.

items.q: Which statement about the proposed AGM date is correct?
o: Invalid: beyond 6 months of FY-end and 15 months from last AGM
Valid: an AGM can be held any time in the calendar year
Valid: the 15 months are counted from the end of the FY
Valid: the Board may extend the date if accounts aren't ready
items.why: Sec 96: the AGM must be held within 6 months of FY-end (30 Sept 2026), and the gap between two AGMs cannot exceed 15 months (30 Dec 2026). 31 Dec 2026 breaches both. Only the ROC can extend, by up to 3 months.
items.trap: It misses the 15-month limit by just one day. Count carefully.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Aarav Sharma

caseBlocks.p: During P.Y. 2025-26, Mr. Aarav sold listed shares (STT paid) for ₹15,00,000. These were bonus shares received on 31.01.2018; FMV on that date was ₹10,00,000. He also incurred a loss of ₹2,00,000 from trading in eligible derivatives on a recognised stock exchange.

items.q: What amount is includible under the head 'Capital Gains'?
items.why: For bonus shares acquired before 1.2.2018, the cost is the FMV on 31.1.2018: ₹10,00,000. LTCG = ₹5,00,000. Eligible derivative trading on a recognised exchange is a non-speculative business u/s 43(5), so the loss goes to PGBP.
items.trap: The derivative loss looks like a capital loss, but it belongs under PGBP.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.title: Aravali Ventures Pvt. Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Aravali Ventures' GTA division transported office furniture by road for the Public Works Department (PWD) of the Rajasthan Government. PWD is registered under GST only for deducting TDS u/s 51, not for making taxable supplies.

items.q: Which statement is most appropriate?
o: Taxable – AVPL pays GST under forward charge as GTA
Taxable – PWD pays under RCM as a registered recipient
Taxable – PWD pays under RCM as a State Govt department
Exempt – GST payable neither by AVPL nor by PWD
items.why: GTA services to a Government department registered only for TDS u/s 51 are exempt.
items.trap: Registration for TDS alone does not make PWD a 'registered recipient' for RCM on GTA.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.title: Sunrise Fabricators Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Sunrise Fabricators pays a guaranteed ₹90 per hour. The standard time for a product is 4 hours. Mr. R, paid under the Rowan plan, earned an effective hourly rate of ₹112.50 on this product.

items.q: Had Mr. R been on the Halsey scheme (50%), what would his total earnings and effective hourly rate be?
items.why: Rowan: 112.5 = 90 + (4 − T)/4 × 90, so T = 3 hours. Halsey: 3 × 90 + 50% × 1 hour × 90 = ₹315, which is ₹105 per hour.
items.trap: First find the actual time from the Rowan rate. Don't assume 4 hours.

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: Arnav Engineering Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Arnav Engineering holds inventory at its own premises and at third-party warehouses, is involved in legal cases with customers and suppliers, and reports segment information. The partner asks the team to apply SA 501.

items.q: As per SA 501, what is the auditor's objective for inventory, litigation and segments, respectively?
items.why: SA 501: existence and condition of inventory; completeness of litigation and claims; presentation and disclosure of segment information.
items.trap: 'Valuation' sounds natural for inventory, but SA 501 targets existence and condition.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Solaris Components Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: The EV-charging project of Solaris Components will be financed at 40% debt and 60% equity. Pre-tax cost of debt is 10%, tax rate 30%, and the project's cost of equity is 16%. (Solaris's existing WACC is 11.32%.)

items.q: What is the project-specific WACC?
items.trap: 11.32% is the firm's existing WACC, which is wrong for a riskier project.

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: Garud AI

caseBlocks.p: In 2024, Garud AI took its existing AI automation products to Dubai and Singapore, chosen for strong digital infrastructure, business-friendly rules and high-value enterprise clients. Revenue rose 25% within a year.

items.q: Which growth strategy did Garud pursue?
items.why: Existing products in new geographic markets is market development.
items.trap: Market penetration means selling more in existing markets.

items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.title: Delma Infrastructure Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Delma Infrastructure Ltd. (DIL) holds 25% of the equity of Bela Ltd. The investment was acquired and is held temporarily for resale, and it is expected to be disposed of within 6 months. DIL prepares consolidated financial statements.

items.q: How should DIL treat its stake in Bela Ltd. in the consolidated financial statements?
o: Not equity-accounted; held exclusively for disposal (AS 13)
Include it as an associate using the equity method
Treat it as a joint venture: proportionate consolidation
Fully consolidate it as a subsidiary
items.why: When an investment is acquired and held exclusively with a view to its subsequent disposal in the near future, the equity method is not applied. It is accounted for under AS 13.
items.trap: The 25% holding tempts you towards 'associate', but the purpose of holding decides.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Aarav Renewable Energy Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: AREL manufactures solar-energy equipment. It now wants to manufacture electric vehicles, an activity outside both the main and the ancillary objects in its Memorandum. The Board says this is 'incidental' to the existing business and can start without altering the MoA.

items.q: Can AREL start manufacturing electric vehicles without altering its Memorandum of Association?
o: Yes – any activity linked to the business is automatically allowed
Yes – if the Board passes a resolution approving the activity
No – a public company can never alter its objects clause
No – it must first alter its objects clause as per the Act
items.why: An activity outside the objects stated in the MoA cannot be undertaken until the objects clause is altered by special resolution under sec 13, following the prescribed procedure.
items.trap: A Board resolution cannot override the Memorandum.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Saksham

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Saksham (50) has opted OUT of the default tax regime for P.Y. 2025-26.

b: Life insurance premiums paid: well above ₹1.5 lakh (all eligible)
Mediclaim (by cheque): wife (47) ₹13,500; mother (70) ₹26,670
Preventive health check-up (cash): ₹5,500 each for wife and mother
Medical expenses (credit card): mother ₹17,000; father (73, uninsured) ₹27,000
Savings bank interest ₹16,000

items.q: What is the total deduction available under Chapter VI-A?
items.why: 80C: ₹1,50,000 (cap). 80D self/family: 13,500 + 5,000 check-up = 18,500. 80D senior parents: 26,670 + father's medical expenses 27,000 = 53,670, capped at 50,000. 80TTA: ₹10,000. Total = ₹2,28,500.
items.trap: The ₹5,000 preventive check-up cap is for the whole family. The mother's medical expenses don't count, as she is insured.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.title: Mr. Venugopal

caseBlocks.p: Venugopal & Co. (Kerala) registered under GST in May. In June:

b: Supplied stock worth ₹1,50,000 to an unregistered buyer. Stock worth ₹50,000 out of this was returned in August.
Sold agricultural land for ₹10,25,000.
Paid ₹10,000 shop rent to the local Municipal Corporation, and ₹20,000 rent for his own residential house.

items.q: What is the value of his outward supply for June?
items.why: Only the stock supplied (₹1,50,000) is an outward supply in June. Sale of land is neither goods nor services (Schedule III). Rent paid is an inward supply. The August return is adjusted later through a credit note.
items.trap: Do not reduce June's value for goods returned in August.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.topic: ABC – Activity cost of a customer
items.title: Kaveri Consumer Durables Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Kaveri's customer Sahyadri Electronics Mart (SEM): 13,500 units sold; 15 purchase orders; 2 customer visits; 10 deliveries of 20 km each; no expedited deliveries.
Rates: order taking ₹13,500/order; visit ₹10,800; delivery ₹22.50 per km; product handling ₹67.50/unit; expedited delivery ₹40,500.

items.q: What is the total customer-level operating activities cost of SEM?
items.trap: Delivery cost is per km travelled, not per delivery.

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: MNO Hospitality Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: At MNO Hospitality, discounted room rates are often given without documented approval. Housekeeping occupancy reports are not retained, and the guest register can be reconciled with bills only for a few dates.

items.q: What is the most critical audit concern?
o: Overstatement of room revenue due to duplicate billing
Revenue leakage; completeness and accuracy can't be verified
Minor timing differences due to delayed reconciliation
Misclassification between room and other operating income
items.why: Unapproved discounts plus missing occupancy records mean revenue may be lost or understated, and its completeness and accuracy cannot be verified.
items.trap: The risk here is understatement (leakage), not overstatement.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Orion Manufacturing Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Orion is comparing two machines (5-year life, straight-line depreciation, no salvage). Annual profit after tax: X-Pro ₹1,71,500 (cost ₹20,00,000); Z-Elite ₹1,92,500 (cost ₹25,00,000).

items.q: What is the ARR on average investment?
items.trap: Dividing by the full cost halves the ARR.

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: EV manufacturer

caseBlocks.p: A premium electric car maker keeps reducing manufacturing cost because its engineers improve battery assembly techniques after every production cycle. The cost reduction comes from accumulated knowledge, not from higher production volume.

items.q: This phenomenon is known as:
items.why: The experience curve: unit costs fall as cumulative experience and learning grow.
items.trap: Economies of scale come from volume, and the case rules volume out.

items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.topic: AS 2 – Normal loss and cost per kg
items.title: Anshul Manufacturers

caseBlocks.p: Anshul Manufacturers' total cost of 20,000 kg of raw material (net of GST credit, including transit cost) is ₹36,00,000. Normal transit loss is 3%. It actually received 19,000 kg.

items.q: What is the cost per kg of raw material as per AS 2?
items.why: Normal loss is absorbed by good units: 36,00,000 ÷ (20,000 − 3% = 19,400 kg) = ₹185.5 (approx.).
items.trap: ₹189.4 divides by 19,000 kg and wrongly loads the abnormal loss into cost.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Mr. A's proposed LLP

caseBlocks.p: In Mr. A's LLP, Mr. B stayed in India for 110 days last year and was not resident. In the next financial year, Mr. B stays in India for 130 days.

items.q: Which of the following is correct for that next financial year?
o: Mr. B still cannot be treated as resident for the LLP Act
Residency is tested only once, at incorporation
He now qualifies as a resident designated partner
Only a partner who has always been resident qualifies
items.why: 130 days meets the 120-day test for that financial year, so Mr. B becomes resident and can serve as the resident designated partner.
items.trap: Residency is tested year by year.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Aarav Sharma

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Aarav (default tax regime), P.Y. 2025-26: salary as ship crew ₹25,00,000. Remuneration as a working partner of a firm ₹5,00,000 (allowed in the firm's hands). Loss from trading in eligible derivatives on a recognised stock exchange ₹2,00,000.

items.q: What is his income under 'Salaries' and 'Profits and gains of business or profession'?
items.why: Salary 25,00,000 − 75,000 standard deduction (default regime) = 24,25,000. Partner's remuneration is PGBP (5,00,000), set off against the non-speculative derivative loss (2,00,000), giving 3,00,000.
items.trap: Partner's remuneration is never 'salary' in the partner's hands.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.title: Aravali Ventures Pvt. Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Aravali Ventures let out three flats in Jaipur:

b: Flat A: to Mr. Sandeep, an unregistered salaried chef, as his residence
Flat B: to Ruhaan Ltd. (registered), to house its manager
Flat C: to Mr. Rohit, a registered proprietor, for his family's residence in his personal capacity; rent paid personally

items.q: Which treatment is correct?
o: Flat A – taxable; AVPL pays GST under forward charge
Flat B – exempt, as the manager using it is unregistered
Flat C – taxable; Mr. Rohit pays GST under RCM
Flat A – exempt, let to an unregistered person as residence
items.why: Renting a residential dwelling for residence is exempt unless it is let to a registered person. Flat B is taxable (Ruhaan pays under RCM). Flat C is exempt, because a registered proprietor taking it in his personal capacity for his own residence is covered.
items.trap: Being registered does not make Flat C taxable.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.title: Alpha Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Alpha Ltd.'s Process Q receives 9,000 kg from Process P. Normal wastage is 10% of input. Actual output transferred to Process R is 8,200 kg.

items.q: What does Process Q show?
items.why: Normal output = 9,000 − 900 = 8,100 kg. Actual output 8,200 kg gives an abnormal gain of 100 kg.
items.trap: Normal loss is 10% of Q's own input (9,000 kg).

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: Arnav Engineering Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: At Arnav Engineering's inventory count: physical quantities differ from perpetual records; goods received on consignment are stored with own goods; some goods are lying with third parties; and receiving and dispatch documents around year-end are not reconciled.

items.q: Which procedures best address these concerns?
o: Cut-off tests, reconcile records, verify consignment and third-party stock
Inspect condition, review valuation, compute turnover, compare margins
Reperform valuation, inspect condition, analyse ratios, review provisions
Inspect damaged items, confirm balances, review obsolescence, check sales
items.why: The issues are quantity, ownership and cut-off. The procedures must target exactly those: cut-off testing, reconciliation, segregation of consignment stock and verification of third-party stock.
items.trap: The other options deal with valuation, which is not the issue raised.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Solaris Components Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Solaris's EV project (₹ crore): machinery 200 (4-year life, straight-line to nil) and working capital 20, recovered in year 4. Year-4 EBITDA is 70 and tax is 30%. The machinery is sold at the end of year 4 for 20 (taxable gain).

items.q: What is the total cash inflow in Year 4, including terminal items?
items.why: Depreciation 50. PBT 20, tax 6, PAT 14, CFAT 64. Add WC 20 and after-tax salvage 14 (20 × 0.70) = ₹98 crore.
items.trap: ₹104 crore ignores tax on the salvage (book value is nil).

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: Garud AI

caseBlocks.p: Garud AI acquired VoiceVerse (speech recognition) and DataPredict (predictive analytics), integrated their technology into its AI solutions, and extended them to new markets.

items.q: Which area of core competence does this illustrate?
items.why: A core competence should give access to a wide variety of markets. Extending integrated capabilities to new markets is the 'application to other markets' test.
items.trap: Differentiation is about rivals. The case is about reach into new markets.

items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.title: Classifying a foreign operation

caseBlocks.p: A reporting enterprise has four foreign operations. You must classify them under AS 11 'The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates'.

items.q: Which of the following is a 'non-integral foreign operation' as per AS 11?
o: A branch that only sells goods imported from the parent and remits proceeds
A branch acting only as a selling agent of the parent on commission
A branch that borrows from the parent to finance all its activities
One that operates largely independently, mainly in local currency
items.why: A non-integral foreign operation accumulates cash and monetary items, incurs expenses, generates income and arranges borrowings largely in its local currency, with a significant degree of autonomy from the reporting enterprise.
items.trap: The other three depend on the parent for everything, so they are integral operations.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Aarav Renewable Energy Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: AREL, a public company, has 900 members. At its AGM, 35 members are personally present. Mr. Rohan (8% holder) has appointed a proxy, deposited 2 days before the meeting. The Chairman says the meeting cannot proceed because proxies are not counted for quorum.

items.q: Is the Chairman right?
o: Yes – proxies are not counted, so the meeting must be adjourned
No – proxy valid but not counted; 35 present exceeds quorum of 5
No – a proxy is always counted for quorum, whatever the Articles say
Yes – only a director or a member can be appointed as a proxy
items.why: Sec 103: a public company with up to 1,000 members needs 5 members personally present. Proxies are not counted, but 35 is far above 5. The proxy is valid (sec 105), as it was deposited at least 48 hours before the meeting.
items.trap: The Chairman is right that proxies are not counted, but wrong about the result.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Saksham

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Saksham (opted out of the default regime), P.Y. 2025-26:

b: LTCG on listed equity shares (STT paid) ₹6,54,000
Dividend ₹12,00,000
Savings bank interest ₹16,000; FD interest ₹45,000
Chapter VI-A deductions ₹2,28,500

items.q: What is his total income for A.Y. 2026-27?
items.why: Salary 45,00,000 − 50,000 standard deduction (old regime) = 44,50,000. Add LTCG 6,54,000, dividend 12,00,000 and interest 61,000 to get GTI 63,65,000. Less deductions 2,28,500 = ₹61,36,500.
items.trap: The standard deduction is ₹50,000 under the old regime, not ₹75,000.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.title: Ganesh & Sons

caseBlocks.p: On 25-04-2025, Ganesh & Sons (Odisha) supplied goods to Mr. Aseem in Kerala for ₹55,000 (excluding GST), of which ₹10,000 are exempt goods shown separately on a single invoice. IGST 18%.

items.q: What is the consignment value for e-way bill purposes?
items.why: Consignment value = taxable value + tax, excluding the exempt supply when both are on one invoice: 45,000 + 18% = ₹53,100.
items.trap: ₹64,900 applies 18% to the full ₹55,000, including exempt goods.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.topic: Cost sheet – Cost of goods sold
items.title: Sunrise Industries Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Sunrise Industries, August 2026 (₹):

b: Raw materials: opening 1,38,000; closing 1,15,000; purchases 11,04,000
WIP: opening 27,600; closing 34,500
Finished goods: opening 2,07,000; closing 2,53,000
Wages 5,52,000; factory overheads 2,30,000; administration overheads (related to production) 1,15,000

items.q: What is the cost of goods sold for August 2026?
items.why: Materials consumed 11,27,000 + wages 5,52,000 = prime cost 16,79,000. Add FOH (19,09,000), adjust WIP (19,02,100), add admin OH (cost of production 20,17,100), adjust FG (+2,07,000 − 2,53,000) = ₹19,71,100.
items.trap: ₹20,17,100 is the cost of production. You still need to adjust finished goods.

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: Bell Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: During the audit of Bell Ltd., several trade receivables have been outstanding for a long time, and some customers dispute the amounts. Management still shows them at their original amounts. The auditor wants to check whether they are recoverable and properly adjusted.

items.q: Which assertion is the auditor primarily verifying?
items.why: Whether receivables are recoverable and appropriately adjusted (for example, allowance for doubtful debts) is the valuation and allocation assertion.
items.trap: The receivables exist. The question is whether they are worth their stated amount.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Orion Manufacturing Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Orion's machine X-Pro costs ₹20,00,000 and generates an annual cash inflow after tax of ₹5,71,500 for 5 years. Required return 12% (PVIFA 12%, 5 years = 3.605).

items.q: What is the Profitability Index of X-Pro?
items.trap: Use CFAT, not PAT.

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: Indian EV manufacturer

caseBlocks.p: An Indian EV maker sees international automobile companies rapidly entering the domestic market, while government incentives for EV manufacturing keep increasing. Management decides to speed up capacity expansion before competition intensifies.

items.q: Which strategic driver is primarily influencing this decision?
items.why: New entrants and changing government incentives are industry and market forces, and they drive the expansion decision.
items.trap: Nothing in the case is about customer needs or channels.

items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.title: Delma Infrastructure Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Delma Infrastructure Ltd. holds 18% in Orion Estates Ltd. It has a board seat, but every decision needs a 3/4th majority and it does not actively take part in policy-making. The CFO asks what actually proves significant influence.

items.q: Which factor BEST indicates significant influence as per AS 23?
o: Holding more than 10% of the voting power
A long-standing trade relationship with the investee
Board seat, policy participation and material transactions
Providing management services to the investee
items.why: AS 23 lists board representation, participation in policy-making, material transactions, interchange of managerial personnel and provision of essential technical information as evidence.
items.trap: The presumption is at 20%, not 10%, and even 20% can be rebutted.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Assertion – Reason

caseBlocks.p: Assertion (A): A partner of an LLP is not personally liable for the wrongful act or omission of any other partner. However, a partner is personally liable for his own wrongful act or omission.
Reason (R): Every partner of an LLP is an agent of the LLP for the purpose of its business, but not an agent of the other partners.

items.q: Select the correct option:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.why: Sec 26 makes every partner an agent of the LLP, not of the other partners. Sec 28 says a partner is not personally liable for another partner's wrongful act, but is liable for his own. R explains A.
items.trap: In a traditional partnership firm, partners are agents of each other. Don't carry that into LLPs.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Aarav Sharma

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Aarav (default regime), P.Y. 2025-26:

b: Income under Salaries ₹24,25,000
LTCG on listed shares ₹5,00,000
Savings bank interest ₹12,500
On 1 Nov 2025 he gifted ₹10,00,000 to his wife, who invested it the same day in an FD @ 6% p.a.

items.q: What is the total income of Mr. Aarav for A.Y. 2026-27?
items.trap: ₹32,37,500 forgets clubbing of the wife's FD interest.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.title: Aravali Ventures Pvt. Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Aravali Ventures' R&D unit is a recognised incubatee at Shekhawati Innovation Foundation, a sec 8 company and a Technology Business Incubator (TBI) recognised by NSTEDB, DST. The TBI provides lab space, mentoring and prototyping, and charges a nominal facility fee.

items.q: Which statement is most appropriate for the TBI's services to AVPL?
o: Taxable at the applicable rate, as a fee is charged
Exempt – services by an NSTEDB-recognised TBI to incubatees
Taxable under RCM in AVPL's hands, being an incubatee
Exempt only if AVPL is not registered under GST
items.why: Services provided by a TBI recognised by NSTEDB (DST, Government of India) to its incubatees are exempt, even though a fee is charged.
items.trap: A nominal fee does not make the service taxable here.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.title: Kaveri Consumer Durables Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Kaveri buys an AC at ₹16,200. Customer Deccan Home Appliances (DHA): 18,000 units at an actual price of ₹19,116; 25 purchase orders; 3 visits; 30 deliveries of 6 km each; no expedited deliveries.
Rates: order ₹13,500; visit ₹10,800; delivery ₹22.50/km; handling ₹67.50/unit.

items.q: What is DHA's customer-level operating income?
items.trap: ₹5,24,88,000 is the gross margin before activity costs.

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: Arnav Engineering Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Arnav Engineering has operating losses, negative cash flows and net current liabilities. Term loans for long-term assets are maturing with no renewal plan. Lenders' support depends on targets, and creditors are paid late. It has also lost a major customer, a key supplier now wants cash-on-delivery, and a new competitor has entered. Management 'expects' new finance.

items.q: What is the most appropriate assessment?
o: Negative cash flows alone prove it; finance plans need no review
Loan maturities matter most; operating events are less relevant
Events, alone or together, may cast significant doubt on going concern
Finance plans remove the doubt unless a loan default has occurred
items.why: SA 570 lists financial and operating events that may, individually or collectively, cast significant doubt. Management's plans must be evaluated, not simply accepted.
items.trap: Management's expectation of finance is not evidence.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Solaris Components Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Solaris's EV project, Year 2 (₹ crore): sales 250; variable costs 60% of sales; fixed cash operating costs 20; depreciation 50.

items.q: Using EBIT after depreciation, what is the DOL, and the effect of a 9% fall in sales on EBIT?
items.why: Contribution 100; EBIT = 100 − 20 − 50 = 30. DOL = 100 ÷ 30 = 3.33. A 9% fall in sales means EBIT falls 3.33 × 9% = 30%.
items.trap: Depreciation is a fixed cost too. Include it when computing EBIT.

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: InnovateCo

caseBlocks.p: InnovateCo's EV division has a low current market share, so BCG classifies it as a 'Question Mark'. The ADL matrix labels the same division 'Dominant', because of its strong industry position and technological leadership. This mismatch is making management rethink resource allocation.

items.q: What contradiction does InnovateCo face?
o: Consumer electronics unit is classified differently in both
Home appliances is labelled both 'Dog' and 'Dominant'
The ADL matrix undervalues the contribution of 'Stars'
EV unit: weak share under BCG, yet strong position under ADL
items.why: BCG uses market growth and relative market share. ADL uses competitive position and industry maturity. The EV unit scores differently on these different metrics.
items.trap: The contradiction is about the EV unit, not the other divisions.

items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.title: Anshul Manufacturers

caseBlocks.p: Anshul Manufacturers expected to receive 19,400 kg of raw material after a normal transit loss of 3% on 20,000 kg, but actually received 19,000 kg. The cost per kg (after absorbing normal loss) is ₹185.5.

items.q: What amount of abnormal loss will be debited to the P&L (approx.)?
items.trap: ₹72,000 values the loss at ₹180, without absorbing the normal loss.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Aarav Renewable Energy Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Members of AREL declared a final dividend of ₹2 crore at the AGM. Due to an oversight, the amount was not deposited in a separate bank account. The finance team proposes to use it temporarily for working capital and restore it before paying shareholders.

items.q: Which statement is correct?
o: Deposit in a separate scheduled bank account within 5 days; can't use it
Once declared, the company may use the amount until the payment date
The separate account rule applies only to listed companies
Temporary use is allowed if the Board resolves to restore it in time
items.why: Sec 123(4): the dividend amount must be deposited in a separate account with a scheduled bank within 5 days of declaration, and it can be used only for paying the dividend.
items.trap: A Board assurance to restore the money is irrelevant. The law prohibits the use itself.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Saksham

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Saksham (50), default tax regime, P.Y. 2025-26: salary ₹45,00,000; dividend ₹12,00,000; interest (SB + FD) ₹61,000; LTCG on listed equity shares (STT paid) ₹6,54,000.

items.q: What is his tax liability for A.Y. 2026-27 under sec 115BAC?
items.trap: Total income is ₹63.4 lakh, so the 10% surcharge applies.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.title: Ganesh & Sons

caseBlocks.p: Ganesh & Sons (registered in Bhubaneswar, Odisha) took a new warehouse on rent near its factory for storage and dispatch. Goods (up to ₹5 lakh per trip) move between the factory and warehouse in a non-motorised cart. Rent is ₹18 lakh for 11 months, then ₹21 lakh.

items.q: Which statement about the new warehouse is most appropriate?
o: Register as a casual taxable person for the lease term
Separate registration once rent exceeds ₹20 lakh a year
Separate GST registration is not mandatory
items.why: The warehouse is an additional place of business in the same State. It is added to the existing registration by amendment. A separate registration is optional.
items.trap: The rent figures are a distractor. Rent has nothing to do with registration.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.title: Alpha Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Alpha Ltd.'s Process Q: input 9,000 kg from P @ ₹15.50 (₹1,39,500); direct material ₹42,500; direct labour ₹40,000; overheads ₹30,000. Normal wastage 10%, scrap ₹1/kg. Actual output 8,200 kg.

items.q: What is the cost per kg of output of Process Q?
items.why: Total cost 2,52,000 − scrap 900 = 2,51,100 ÷ normal output 8,100 kg = ₹31.00. The abnormal gain is valued at ₹31.
items.trap: ₹30.73 divides by actual output (8,200 kg).

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: MNO Hospitality Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: With KOTs, occupancy reports and guest billing trails missing, MNO Hospitality's auditor relies on internally generated system summaries (with weak underlying controls), oral explanations from staff, and photocopies and system extracts instead of originals.

items.q: How is the reliability of this audit evidence best evaluated?
o: Sufficient – oral explanations backed by internal summaries
Fully reliable – internally generated reports are always reliable
Less reliable – weak controls and uncorroborated oral representations
Equal to originals – copies and summaries serve the same purpose
items.why: SA 500: evidence is more reliable when controls are effective, when it is documentary rather than oral, and when it is original rather than a copy. All three fail here.
items.trap: Two weak sources do not add up to one strong source.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Orion Manufacturing Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Orion's machine Z-Elite costs ₹25,00,000. Annual PAT is ₹1,92,500 and depreciation ₹5,00,000, for 5 years. Required return 12% (PVIFA 12%, 5 years = 3.605).

items.q: What is the Profitability Index of Z-Elite?
items.trap: Z-Elite saves more in wages, yet X-Pro has the better PI (1.03).

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: Consumer electronics company

caseBlocks.p: A consumer electronics company permanently discontinues its MP3 player business because of continuously declining demand and growing losses. The resources released are invested in wearable technology.

items.q: This decision primarily represents:
items.why: Permanently withdrawing from a business is a strategic exit (divestment), a form of retrenchment.
items.trap: Reinvesting in wearables is a consequence. The decision itself is the exit.

items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.title: Delma Infrastructure Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Delma Infrastructure Ltd. holds 30% of Sima Developers Pvt. Ltd., sits on its board and takes part in policy decisions. Sima is therefore an associate. DIL also has jointly controlled entities, accounted for under AS 27.

items.q: How should DIL account for Sima Developers in its consolidated financial statements?
o: At cost, as a long-term investment
As a financial asset at fair value
items.why: AS 23 requires the equity method for an associate in the consolidated financial statements.
items.trap: Proportionate consolidation is for jointly controlled entities (AS 27), not associates.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Mr. A's proposed LLP

caseBlocks.p: Mr. A applied to the Registrar for reservation of the desired name of his LLP and paid the fee. The Registrar approved the name on 3 April 2026.

items.q: For how long will the approved name remain reserved from the date of intimation by the Registrar?
items.why: Under the LLP Rules, an approved name is reserved for 3 months from the date of intimation by the Registrar.
items.trap: Do not mix this up with the name reservation periods for companies.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Aarav Sharma

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Aarav's total income for A.Y. 2026-27 (default regime) is ₹32,62,500. This includes LTCG u/s 112A of ₹5,00,000 on listed shares (STT paid). Ignore TDS/TCS.

items.q: What is Mr. Aarav's tax liability for A.Y. 2026-27?
items.trap: Don't forget the ₹1.25 lakh exemption on 112A gains.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.topic: Value of supply – subsidies, late fee
items.title: Aravali Ventures Pvt. Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Aravali Ventures' herbal tonic sales in July (excl. GST; normal price ₹300/unit):

b: 5,000 units to Bharat Pharma @ ₹300. A late fee of ₹1,500 was levied and then waived in the same month.
2,000 units to EWS families @ ₹150; the State Government pays the balance ₹150/unit as a price-linked subsidy.
480 units to an old age home @ ₹250. An NGO separately gave a lump-sum ₹30,000 subsidy to recognise AVPL's service to the elderly.

items.q: What is the value of taxable supply for July?
items.why: 15,00,000 (late fee waived, so not charged) + 3,00,000 (Government subsidy excluded u/s 15(2)(e)) + 1,20,000 (NGO lump-sum not linked to price) = ₹19,20,000.
items.trap: ₹19,21,500 adds the waived late fee.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.title: Kaveri Consumer Durables Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Kaveri buys an AC at ₹16,200. Its biggest customer, Shivneri Retail Hub (SRH): 38,250 units at an actual price of ₹17,496; 30 orders; 3 visits; 20 deliveries of 30 km each; 2 expedited deliveries.
Rates: order ₹13,500; visit ₹10,800; delivery ₹22.50/km; handling ₹67.50/unit; expedited ₹40,500 each.

items.q: What is SRH's customer-level operating income?
items.trap: SRH buys twice DHA's volume but earns less than DHA's ₹5.09 crore. Big discounts and expensive deliveries eat the margin.

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: Arnav Engineering Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: On the audit team: Mr. S ignored materially misleading information in the audit documentation. Mr. R gave in to senior management pressure on a key judgement. Mr. A lacked the required skill and performed an important procedure carelessly. Mr. M plans to share client information with a third party without authority.

items.q: Which principles did Mr. S, Mr. R, Mr. A and Mr. M compromise, respectively?
o: Objectivity, Integrity, Prof. Competence & Due Care, Prof. Behaviour
Integrity, Objectivity, Prof. Competence & Due Care, Confidentiality
Prof. Behaviour, Objectivity, Integrity, Prof. Competence & Due Care
items.why: Being associated with misleading information is Integrity. Undue influence is Objectivity. Lack of skill and care is Professional Competence & Due Care. Unauthorised disclosure is Confidentiality.
items.trap: Pressure from management is an Objectivity issue, not Integrity.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Solaris Components Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Solaris's EV project: initial outlay ₹220 crore. Cash inflows (₹ crore): Y1 50, Y2 71, Y3 78, Y4 98. Project WACC 12.40%; PVIF: 0.890, 0.792, 0.704, 0.627. (At the firm's WACC of 11.32%, NPV would be +₹2.55 crore.)

items.q: What is the NPV at the project-specific WACC, and the decision?
items.trap: Using the firm's WACC would wrongly accept a project with higher business risk.

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: Garud AI

caseBlocks.p: After its acquisitions and merger, Garud AI runs AI solutions and legacy IT services. It wants separate business units, each with its own functional specialists and clear responsibility for performance.

items.q: Which organisational structure is most appropriate?
items.why: A divisional structure groups activities by product or business. Each division has its own specialists and is accountable for its results.
items.trap: Matrix means dual reporting, the opposite of single clear accountability.

items.subject: Advanced Accounting
items.title: Anshul Manufacturers

caseBlocks.p: Anshul Manufacturers received 19,000 kg of raw material, and the cost per kg as per AS 2 is ₹185.5. During the year, it consumed 17,600 kg. There was no opening stock.

items.q: What will be the value of closing stock of raw material?
items.trap: ₹2,38,000 values the stock at the gross price of ₹170.

items.subject: Corporate & Other Laws
items.title: Aarav Renewable Energy Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: During AREL's statutory audit, the auditor has reason to believe that the CFO manipulated invoices and overstated expenses by ₹75 lakh, a suspected fraud by an officer of the company.

items.q: What is the auditor's obligation under sec 143(12) read with Rule 13?
o: Report to the Central Government in ADT-4, whatever the amount
None – fraud below ₹1 crore needs no reporting at all
Report to Audit Committee/Board; disclosed in Board's Report
Report only if shareholders pass a resolution authorising it
items.why: For fraud below ₹1 crore, the auditor reports to the Audit Committee (or the Board), and the company discloses it in the Board's Report. Fraud of ₹1 crore or more goes to the Central Government in ADT-4.
items.trap: 'Below ₹1 crore' changes whom the auditor reports to. It does not remove the duty to report.

items.subject: Taxation – Income Tax
items.title: Mr. Saksham

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Saksham (50) has opted out of the default regime. His total income for A.Y. 2026-27 is ₹61,36,500. This includes LTCG u/s 112A of ₹6,54,000 on listed equity shares (STT paid).

items.q: What is his tax liability for A.Y. 2026-27?
items.trap: Insight: the default regime (₹15,46,600) saves him about ₹1.96 lakh.

items.subject: Taxation – GST
items.title: Mr. Ramesh

caseBlocks.p: Mr. Ramesh, a regular GST taxpayer filing returns u/s 39(1), had his registration cancelled with effect from 10th July. The cancellation order was issued on 25th July.

items.q: By when must Mr. Ramesh file his final return (GSTR-10)?
items.why: Sec 45: the final return is due within 3 months of the date of cancellation or the date of the cancellation order, whichever is later. 25 July + 3 months = 25 October.
items.trap: Counting from 10 July gives 10 October, which is wrong.

items.subject: Cost & Management Accounting
items.title: Alpha Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Alpha Ltd.'s Process R: input 8,200 kg from Q @ ₹31; direct material ₹42,880; direct labour ₹50,000; overheads ₹37,500. Normal wastage 10%, scrap ₹1/kg. Output 7,300 kg goes to the warehouse. The price must give a 25% profit on selling price.

items.q: What should the selling price per kg of the finished product be?
items.trap: ₹65 is 25% on cost, not 25% on selling price.

items.subject: Auditing & Ethics
items.title: MNO Hospitality Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Several banquet events at MNO Hospitality were held before year-end but invoiced after it. Some of this revenue was booked without invoices, while post-year-end invoices were included in year-end receivables without support. Event records and invoicing were not reconciled.

items.q: What is the most appropriate audit conclusion?
o: Cut-off error – possible misstatement of revenue and receivables
Receivables are understated due to delayed invoicing
A cut-off error affecting only revenue recognised for the period
A cut-off error affecting only trade receivables at year-end
items.why: Inconsistent recognition plus unsupported receivables is a cut-off error that can misstate both revenue (completeness/occurrence) and receivables (existence).
items.trap: Options B and C each show only half of the impact.

items.subject: Financial Management
items.title: Solaris Components Ltd.

caseBlocks.p: Solaris's existing business: EBIT ₹150 crore. Debt (market value) ₹400 crore at a pre-tax cost of 10%. No preference capital.

items.q: What is the DFL, and the effect of a 10% fall in EBIT on EPS?
items.trap: Use pre-tax interest. Tax doesn't change DFL.

items.subject: Strategic Management
items.title: Logistics company

caseBlocks.p: A logistics company regularly monitors technological developments, competitor actions, customer expectations and government policies, even when no specific threat has been identified.

items.q: Which type of strategic control is illustrated?
items.why: Strategic surveillance is broad, general monitoring of events inside and outside the firm that may affect strategy.
items.trap: Premise control checks specific planning assumptions. Special alert reacts to a sudden event.
